headline: Xanadu put a date on 1,000 logical qubits — and published the number it has to fix first
dek: More than 1,000 logical qubits by 2031, fault tolerance in 2028–2029, a quantum data centre by 2030. Also: a photon-loss figure that has to fall from 24.1× to 1.0×. The second number is the honest one.

source.name: The Quantum Insider
source.title: Xanadu Targets More Than 1,000 Logical Qubits by 2031, 31 August 2026 (reporting Xanadu's published roadmap)

body_html:
Xanadu published an updated hardware roadmap: fault tolerance in 2028–2029, a quantum data centre by 2030, and more than 1,000 logical qubits by 2031, with a target logical error rate of 10−16. Separately it is building a photonics research and manufacturing facility, “Inception”, under Project OPTIMISM with CAD $195 million in Canadian federal funding.

Roadmaps are cheap and every vendor has one. What makes this one worth reading is that it names the obstacle in its own units. Xanadu's architecture is photonic, and the dominant error source in photonics is loss — photons that simply do not arrive. The roadmap commits to driving a photon-loss indicator from 24.1× in 2026 down to 1.0× by 2030.

That is the whole difficulty stated as a single number, and stating it is a good sign. A twenty-four-fold reduction in the dominant error channel is the precondition for every qubit figure further along the chart; if it does not arrive on schedule, nothing downstream of it does either. Read the loss curve, not the qubit curve.

What this does NOT mean

  • A roadmap is not a result. This is a dated, public, falsifiable statement about the future — which is to say it is precisely the category the Ledger exists to log the day it is made and resolve when the deadline arrives, rather than let it quietly disappear.
  • 1,000 logical qubits is not comparable across platforms. A photonic logical qubit, a superconducting one and a trapped-ion one are different objects with different codes and different overheads underneath. Comparing the headline counts of two roadmaps built on different modalities is close to meaningless.
  • 10−16 is a target, not a measurement. No hardware has demonstrated it.
  • Funding is not capability. CAD $195M buys a fabrication facility. It does not buy the loss reduction, which is a physics and materials problem.
concept_card_html:
Concepts in this story

Each of these is already explained on SymbiQ. Depth chips say how deep the explanation goes.

  • photonic qubitsworkingRoom temperature and natural networking, fighting loss as the central enemy.
  • logical qubitplainOne reliable qubit built out of many unreliable ones. The only qubit count that means anything.
  • error thresholdworkingThe line the whole field is racing to stay under. Below it, more qubits compound into reliability; above it, more qubits make things worse.
  • fault toleranceformalComputing reliably out of unreliable parts -- the regime the whole roadmap is aimed at.
